user_profile.role: Product/Marketing Data Analyst (Data Analyst/ Analytics / AI Engineer)
user_profile.other_preferences: need a fast job, Intermediate (Built small projects) coding experience, familiar with python, java, c++, R Language. build some academic projects.Preferable language is Python and R

learning_plan.execution_strategy_summary: Alright, future Data Analyst! This isn't just a curriculum; it's *your* personalized sprint to a FAANG-level data role in just 90 days. We're leveraging your strong Computer Science foundation – your logical thinking, your Python proficiency, your comfort with coding, and even your R language familiarity – to accelerate past the basics. We'll aggressively build production-ready skills in advanced SQL, robust Python data manipulation, and critical BI tools like Power BI, all while honing your business acumen for product and marketing insights. Every hour is optimized to transform your academic knowledge into a job-winning portfolio that shouts 'hire me!'

monthly_plan.theme: The Foundation: SQL, Python & Your First Project Steps
weekly_micro_goals: Week 1: You'll dive deep into advanced SQL, mastering complex joins, subqueries, and the powerful world of Window Functions. Your CSE background means we'll skip the basics and immediately focus on the complex query structures and optimization crucial for real-world data extraction. Think about how these can unlock insights from user activity logs.

Week 2: It's all about Python! We're skipping introductory programming and jumping straight into advanced Pandas and NumPy operations, focusing on efficient data manipulation and getting those large datasets ready for action. Your existing Python proficiency will be a massive head start, enabling you to grasp industry-standard data handling techniques rapidly.

Week 3: Continue solidifying your Python data superpowers, tackling performance considerations (vectorization is your friend!) and complex data structures. Concurrently, you'll set up Git and GitHub, integrating version control into your emerging Capstone project from day one. Your prior exposure to version control in CS will make applying Git to data science projects a natural extension.

Week 4: Consolidate your SQL and Python knowledge by applying it to the initial phase of your Capstone project. You'll focus on data acquisition, designing a basic schema for an e-commerce or product usage dataset, and performing initial exploratory data analysis. Simultaneously, start tackling advanced SQL interview questions – pattern recognition is key for those challenging data puzzles!
technical_skills_to_master: Efficiently query and transform complex datasets using advanced SQL constructs (Window Functions, CTEs, complex Joins).
Perform high-performance data manipulation and cleaning using advanced Pandas and NumPy.
Manage project code and collaborate effectively using Git and GitHub.
Design simple relational schemas for analytical purposes and interact with databases programmatically.
interview_prep_goals: Solve 10-15 advanced SQL LeetCode/StrataScratch problems focusing on window functions, joins, and aggregations.
Understand the STAR method for behavioral questions and outline 2-3 relevant academic project experiences that demonstrate problem-solving.
what_you_will_build: A foundational Python script to connect to a simulated PostgreSQL/MySQL database and extract data using your advanced SQL skills.
Initial Pandas DataFrames for your Capstone Project, demonstrating efficient data loading, basic cleaning, and initial transformations for a real-world dataset (e.g., website analytics).
A well-structured GitHub repository for your Capstone project, complete with a professional `README.md` outlining your initial project goals and data sources.
job_hunt_action_items: Optimize your LinkedIn profile with keywords relevant to Product/Marketing Data Analyst roles, explicitly highlighting your CSE background and new technical skills.
Draft a foundational resume, emphasizing your CSE degree and listing Python, SQL, and Git as core technical skills.
Start researching target companies and specific job descriptions to understand common tech stacks and the types of problems they solve for data analysts.

curated_resources.recommended_search_term: Pandas User Guide (GroupBy, Merge, Time Series)

monthly_plan.milestone_deliverable: A GitHub repository for your Capstone project containing initial data ingestion scripts (SQL/Python), a clean `README.md`, and proof of advanced SQL query execution and Pandas data manipulation for initial data exploration.

monthly_plan.theme: Deeper Insights: Statistics, Cleaning, Visualization & Product Sense
weekly_micro_goals: Week 1: We're diving into the heart of data analysis: Probability & Statistics. You'll solidify descriptive and inferential statistics, hypothesis testing (t-tests, chi-squared), and common distributions. Your inherent mathematical and logical reasoning from your CSE degree will be a huge asset in directly applying these statistical concepts to real-world analytical problems like A/B test analysis.

Week 2: Roll up your sleeves for Data Cleaning & Feature Engineering. This is where your coding chops truly shine, transforming raw, messy data into high-quality, analytical-ready assets using Python. Get ready to battle missing values, outliers, and create powerful new features from existing ones. This leverages your coding background to build robust data pipelines!

Week 3: Time to make data speak! You'll master Data Visualization & Storytelling with Matplotlib, Seaborn, and an introduction to interactive tools like Plotly Express. Crucially, you'll learn the *art* of visual communication and crafting a compelling narrative from your data, ensuring your insights resonate with product and marketing stakeholders.

Week 4: Apply your analytical toolkit by focusing on crucial Product & Marketing Analytics Metrics. Define, calculate, and interpret MAU, LTV, conversion funnels, AARRR framework, and more. Simultaneously, master advanced spreadsheet functions for rapid ad-hoc analyses. Your Capstone project will grow significantly with these business-driven insights, directly aligning your technical skills with the demands of a Product/Marketing Data Analyst role.
technical_skills_to_master: Apply core statistical concepts (hypothesis testing, common distributions) to interpret data accurately and drive data-driven decisions.
Independently clean, preprocess, and feature engineer complex datasets using Python, implementing programmatic data quality checks.
Design and create impactful static and interactive data visualizations in Python, adhering to principles of effective visual communication.
Define, calculate, and interpret key product and marketing metrics (e.g., AARRR, LTV, CAC), linking them to business objectives.
Perform complex data analysis and reporting using advanced spreadsheet features (e.g., Pivot Tables, XLOOKUP, Google Sheets QUERY).
interview_prep_goals: Practice case study questions involving metric definition and basic A/B test interpretation.
Solve 10 Python Pandas interview problems focused on cleaning, merging, and grouping data.
Refine your STAR method stories, focusing on data challenges, problem-solving, and your approach to data quality.
what_you_will_build: Comprehensive Python scripts for your Capstone project demonstrating advanced data cleaning, imputation, and feature engineering techniques.
A series of high-quality static and interactive data visualizations in Python that tell a clear story about user behavior or marketing campaign performance within your Capstone.
A spreadsheet model demonstrating advanced formulas and pivot tables for a specific segment of your Capstone data, showcasing rapid ad-hoc analysis skills.
job_hunt_action_items: Start practicing elevator pitches for your Capstone project, emphasizing the business problem it solves and the insights gained.
Identify 5-10 companies where you'd love to work and deeply analyze their job descriptions for common requirements and company culture.
Begin mock behavioral interviews with a peer or mentor, focusing on communicating your impact.

curated_resources.recommended_search_term: Python for Data Analysis by Wes McKinney (Chapter on Data Wrangling)
Storytelling with Data by Cole Nussbaumer Knaflic

monthly_plan.milestone_deliverable: A polished Python notebook for your Capstone project, featuring robust data cleaning, new engineered features, and compelling Python-based visualizations telling a clear analytical story with defined product/marketing metrics, ready for stakeholder presentation.

monthly_plan.theme: Dashboarding, Experimentation, Portfolio & The Job Hunt Sprint
weekly_micro_goals: Week 1: It's time to master Power BI, the industry-standard BI tool. You'll connect various data sources (SQL, CSVs), transform data with Power Query, build robust data models, and learn DAX for powerful calculated columns and measures. This directly addresses a primary skill for your target role, bridging raw analysis with stakeholder-friendly reporting.

Week 2: Deep dive into Statistical Analysis & Experimentation, specifically A/B Testing. You'll learn to design robust experiments, calculate sample sizes, interpret results with confidence intervals and p-values, and make data-driven recommendations. This applies your statistical and programming background to a highly demanded industry skill, enabling you to drive evidence-based product/marketing decisions.

Week 3: Integrate your Power BI and A/B testing knowledge by building a dynamic, interactive dashboard for your Capstone project. You'll finalize your data story, focusing on actionable insights for product and marketing teams, simulating cross-functional collaboration. This week is heavy on presentation skills and refining your project's business impact, leveraging your analytical problem-solving to frame technical findings within a compelling business context.

Week 4: This is the sprint! Polish your Capstone project(s) to perfection – including cloud hosting/deployment, comprehensive documentation, and a killer presentation. Spend significant time on mock interviews (technical & behavioral), tailor your resume for every application, and actively engage in the job hunt, networking relentlessly. This final push integrates all learned skills into cohesive, resume-worthy projects.
technical_skills_to_master: Connect to various data sources in Power BI, perform complex data transformations using Power Query, and build robust data models.
Create advanced calculations using DAX and design interactive, insightful Power BI reports and dashboards, publishing them to Power BI Service.
Design robust A/B tests, analyze and interpret results for statistical significance, and communicate recommendations effectively.
Translate ambiguous business problems into clear analytical questions, develop strong product sense, and communicate complex findings to diverse audiences.
interview_prep_goals: Conduct 3-5 mock technical interviews (SQL, Python, Stats, A/B Testing case studies) with peers or mentors.
Practice explaining your Capstone project end-to-end, focusing on challenges, solutions, business impact, and your decision-making process.
Prepare for common behavioral questions using the STAR method, linking back to your unique CSE background and new data skills, demonstrating structured problem-solving.
what_you_will_build: A fully interactive Power BI dashboard for your Capstone project, deployed to Power BI Service, showcasing key product/marketing metrics and experimentation results.
A simulated A/B test analysis in Python for your Capstone, complete with statistical significance testing and clear, data-driven recommendations and risk assessment.

A compelling, polished presentation of your Capstone project, tailored for both technical and non-technical stakeholders, highlighting actionable insights and potential business impact. This will be hosted on GitHub with detailed `README.md`.
job_hunt_action_items: Finalize and deploy your Capstone project(s) to public platforms (GitHub, Power BI Service, potentially Streamlit for Python apps), ensuring professional documentation.
Tailor your resume and cover letter for 5-10 target roles each week, emphasizing relevant keywords and quantifiable achievements from your projects.
Conduct informational interviews with professionals in target roles/companies to expand your network and gain insights.
Actively apply to 10-15 roles per week, meticulously tracking applications, and proactively reach out to recruiters/hiring managers on LinkedIn.

curated_resources.recommended_search_term: Guy in a Cube Power BI YouTube Channel
Trustworthy Online Controlled Experiments by Kohavi, Tang, Xu

monthly_plan.milestone_deliverable: A complete, deployed, and professionally documented Capstone project (GitHub, Power BI Service) with a compelling presentation, ready to be showcased in interviews. This is your flagship portfolio piece, demonstrating end-to-end analytical capability and business acumen.

critical_guidelines: **The 70/30 Rule is Your Mantra:** For every hour of learning, dedicate 30% to understanding concepts (reading, watching tutorials) and a whopping 70% to active application. This means *doing* – coding, debugging, building, experimenting. No passive learning allowed; your brain truly learns by doing!

**Time-Boxing the Beast:** You *will* hit roadblocks and frustrating bugs. It's normal. If you're stuck on a single problem for more than 45-60 minutes, time-box it. Document what you tried, then move to a different task or seek help. Your goal is forward momentum, not endless frustration.

**Project-First Mindset, No Clichés:** From day one, think about how every new skill fits into your Capstone project. This isn't just about learning; it's about *applying* to solve a real business problem. Forget 'Titanic' datasets; your portfolio will showcase end-to-end, deployable solutions to relevant product/marketing challenges, reflecting real-world impact.

**Embrace the Struggle, Prioritize Recovery:** This pace is intense. There will be days you feel overwhelmed, or a topic seems impossible. That's your brain growing! But remember your buffer hours are sacred. Use them for rest, family, or unexpected life events. Burnout is the enemy of progress; prioritize mental and physical well-being.

**Network Relentlessly:** Learning in a silo is a mistake in the job market. Connect with other aspiring data analysts, engage on LinkedIn, and participate in data communities. Share your project progress, ask questions, and learn from others' journeys. Your next job often comes from who you know and the connections you build.
learning_plan.final_readiness_summary: Upon completing this rigorous 3-month roadmap, you won't just be a CSE graduate; you'll be a highly competitive, production-ready Product/Marketing Data Analyst. Your deep understanding of advanced SQL, Python for data, and Power BI, coupled with a strong grasp of product metrics and A/B testing, will make you an invaluable asset. Your well-documented, end-to-end portfolio projects – built iteratively and leveraging your existing coding prowess – will powerfully demonstrate your ability to translate complex data into actionable business insights. You'll be ready to ace technical interviews, communicate effectively with stakeholders, and hit the ground running in a fast-paced industry role, giving you that 'unfair advantage' you earned.
